Those are **lichen planus** lesions. Flat-topped, purple, polygonal, and pruritic. The shape isn't random.

The mechanism is a **CD8+ T-cell attack on the basal keratinocytes**. The T cells recognize a self-antigen altered by the hepatitis C virus infection. This destroys the basal layer, causing the epidermis to slide off and create the **Wickham striae** — lacy white lines you see on the surface. The polygonal shape comes from the **spatial arrangement of the rete ridges**: the immune attack follows the undulating dermal-epidermal junction, producing angular borders.

Contrast with psoriasis, where the proliferation is uniform and silvery, not flat and purple. At the bedside, if you see **oral lacy plaques** alongside these skin lesions, you can be nearly certain it's hepatitis C driving this. The next step is a **hepatitis C antibody test** to confirm the trigger.

Good question. You're picturing the lesion growing unevenly, like a tumor. That's not it.

The **wavy, polygonal edge** comes from the **anatomy of the rete ridges** themselves. The dermal-epidermal junction is not a flat line. It undulates like interlocking fingers. The **CD8+ T cells attack the basal keratinocytes** only where those cells sit at the tips of the rete ridges. The attack follows that pre-existing wave pattern.

So the lesion doesn't "grow" into a wavy shape. The **immune attack reveals the underlying architecture** of your skin. The flat purple patch is the zone of damage. The wavy border is literally a map of where your rete ridges used to be. That is why you never get a smooth, round border like a nummular eczema patch. The shape is dictated by the **spatial arrangement of the target cells**, not by the direction of growth.

The **Wickham striae** are not the growing edge. They are the **scar of the attack**. The T cells kill the basal keratinocytes. The epidermis above that spot loses its anchor and lifts slightly. The **lacy white lines you see are the thickened granular layer** in the areas where the rete ridges used to dip down. The immune attack spares the tops of the ridges, so the white lines trace the **valleys between the ridges** — the original wavy architecture.

So the lesion is not growing outward in a wave. The **purple patch is the battlefield**. The white lacy lines are the **remnants of the pre-existing skin folds** that the T cells hollowed out. You are not watching cells grow. You are watching the **skeleton of the skin revealed** by selective destruction.

The hepatitis C connection: the virus infects lymphocytes, not skin cells. It **alters the T cell repertoire** so they mistake your own basal keratinocytes for viral antigens. That is why treating the hepatitis C often makes the lichen planus disappear. The T cells stop getting the wrong orders.
